title: Module 3 intro — GPU Acceleration and Optimization

lines: Welcome to Module Three: GPU Acceleration and Optimization.
Here you learn how language models are really trained on GPUs.

say.0: Welcome to Module Three: G P U Acceleration and Optimization.
say.1: Here you learn how language models are really trained on G P Us.

lines: Picture a startup that has just rented eight H100s.
The plan: fully fine-tune a thirteen billion parameter model by Friday.

say.0: Picture a startup that has just rented eight H one hundreds.

lines: The first launch dies in seconds with an out-of-memory error.
Someone halves the batch size, and it crashes exactly the same way.
In bf16, the weights alone are only twenty-six gigabytes.
But AdamW also keeps gradients, a master copy, and two optimizer moments.

say.0: In B F sixteen, the weights alone are only twenty-six gigabytes.
say.1: But Adam W also keeps gradients, a master copy, and two optimizer moments.

lines: That's sixteen bytes per parameter, about two hundred and eight gigabytes.
No single eighty gigabyte GPU holds that, whatever the batch size.

say.1: No single eighty gigabyte G P U holds that, whatever the batch size.

lines: Lesson one teaches this memory math, from optimizer states to the KV cache.
You'll write an estimator that answers "will it fit?" before you launch.

say.0: Lesson one teaches this memory math, from optimizer states to the K V cache.

lines: Lesson two adds mixed precision, gradient accumulation, and activation checkpointing.
FlashAttention and torch.compile then make every step faster.

say.1: Flash Attention and torch dot compile then make every step faster.

lines: In lesson three's lab, you'll pretrain a small Llama from scratch on TinyStories.
You'll watch the loss fall, then generate stories from your own checkpoint.

say.0: In lesson three's lab, you'll pretrain a small Lahma from scratch on Tiny Stories.

lines: Back at the startup, the real fix is sharding.
With FSDP or ZeRO, each GPU keeps only its own slice of the training state.

say.1: With F S D P or zero, each G P U keeps only its own slice of the training state.

lines: Lesson four starts with simple data parallelism, using DDP and torchrun.
Then come tensor and pipeline parallelism, for models too big for one GPU.

say.0: Lesson four starts with simple data parallelism, using D D P and torch run.
say.1: Then come tensor and pipeline parallelism, for models too big for one G P U.

lines: Placement matters: tensor parallelism stays inside a node, on fast NVLink.
Pipeline stages and data-parallel replicas can stretch across nodes over InfiniBand.

say.0: Placement matters: tensor parallelism stays inside a node, on fast N V Link.

lines: The job finally runs, and the dashboard shows 100% GPU utilization.
Yet progress is slow, because the Tensor Cores are mostly waiting.

say.0: The job finally runs, and the dashboard shows one hundred percent G P U utilization.

lines: Lesson five measures real efficiency with model FLOPs utilization, or MFU.
You'll profile steps with PyTorch and Nsight to find the stalls.

say.0: Lesson five measures real efficiency with model flops utilization, or M F U.
say.1: You'll profile steps with pie torch and N sight to find the stalls.

lines: You'll learn an ordered ladder of fixes for out-of-memory errors.
And you'll debug NaN losses, loss spikes, and NCCL hangs.

say.1: And you'll debug nan losses, loss spikes, and nickel hangs.

lines: This domain is fourteen percent of the exam.
Expect memory math, ZeRO stages, parallel layouts, and profiling scenarios.

say.1: Expect memory math, zero stages, parallel layouts, and profiling scenarios.

lines: By the end, you'll size, launch, scale, and debug a real training run.
Let's start with lesson one: GPU memory math.
